title: Fast reactor fuel fabrication
bottleneck: Sodium fast reactors need metallic or nitride fuels that must be fabricated remotely in hot cells because of their radioactivity, a capability that barely exists commercially. The US produced such fuel for the Experimental Breeder Reactor-II decades ago, but the industrial base is gone. Rebuilding remote fuel fabrication at commercial scale is a multi-billion-dollar, decade-long undertaking with its own licensing hurdles.
why_it_blocks: Fast reactors are the path to closing the fuel cycle and burning long-lived waste, but without fuel fabrication infrastructure they cannot be built. The reactor design is the easy part.
current_state: DOE is recovering HALEU from EBR-II fuel at Idaho National Lab as a bridge supply, targeting about 10 metric tons by late 2028. Commercial-scale fast-reactor fuel fabrication does not exist.
